column2: batch 55 — atparl: the Austrian Parliament's materials index, read as seven complete slices.
Measured 2026-10-23. Every row was read BOTH by hand against the endpoint (the probe
column: the upstream's own `count`, `pages` and the distinct count of the record key)
and through the engine (`./bin/japanosint --run <id>` against a scratch database).
The probe sends GET and this endpoint ignores the query string entirely, so
tools/probe_hp_batch.py cannot judge these rows — the by-hand readings are in
docs/at-parlament-filter-api-2026-10-23.md and are reproduced here.
There is no sort parameter on this endpoint and none is needed: `showAll=true` plus a
GP filter is a complete, deterministic, single-page read.

TOTALS: 391357 records emitted, 391357 stored, 7 requests, 222,485,643 bytes, zero notices.
The database holds 391,361 rows for these seven ids — four more than the by-hand counts,
because the open 28th period gained materials between the two readings (26,714 by hand,
26,718 in the engine minutes later). That drift IS the open period, not a gap: the 27 GP
codes' counts summed to 391,354 against an unfiltered 391,354 read in the same minute.
distinct_on_key is GP_CODE+ITYP+INR+NRBR. The obvious key is WRONG and all three obvious
candidates agree on the wrong answer: WENTRY_ID (the site's own web-item id), HIS_URL and
GP_CODE+ITYP+INR each give 75,485 of XXVII's 76,457. All 972 groups DIFFER, in exactly one
column — NRBR — because a material that went through both chambers is served once per
chamber under one web-item id.
